prompt_md: Spinner A gives a uniformly random number from 0 to 1; spinner B, from 0 to 3. A friend picks one at random, spins it twice and gets 0.7 and 0.4. Chance it was A?
prompt_short: Spinner on 0–1 or 0–3, picked at random. Spins 0.7 and 0.4. Chance of A?
hint_md: How likely is each spinner to land that close to 0.7 and 0.4?
explain_intuition_md: Both spinners can produce 0.7 and 0.4, so it feels like a toss-up. But B spreads its results over three times the range, so each of its spins is only a third as likely to land near those values. Two such spins make A nine times as likely, so 9 in 10.
explain_math_md: On $[0,1]$, A has density $1$ and B has density $\tfrac13$: $$P(A \mid \text{spins}) = \frac{1 \cdot 1}{1 \cdot 1 + \tfrac13 \cdot \tfrac13} = \frac{9}{10}$$
